title: Market Orders vs Limit Orders, in Plain Terms
summary: Exchanges generally offer two basic ways to trade. A market order executes immediately at the best prices currently available. A limit order instead states a price, and waits: it only fills at that price or better, and may not fill at all.
blocks: Exchanges generally offer two basic ways to trade. A market order executes immediately at the best prices currently available. A limit order instead states a price, and waits: it only fills at that price or better, and may not fill at all.

The trade-off is speed versus certainty of price. A market order is certain to execute but not certain what it will pay, especially in a fast or thin market. A limit order caps the price but accepts the risk of missing execution entirely if the market never reaches it.

Order books pair these constantly: resting limit orders form the book, and incoming market orders consume them. Understanding which kind an app sends on your behalf explains why a fill sometimes lands away from the last price shown on the chart.
